controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color from its measured spectrum; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 39587). The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,882 K and log g 4.4 (u1 0.438, u2 0.273): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The spin axis's direction on the sky is a display convention.

controls.label: Derived corona
controls.notes: No telescope has imaged this corona, and this is not a published result: it is derived here from the star's magnetic map by a standard method. Gas at rest is placed along the line where the field of the Dec 2014 map reverses, and the wind everywhere else. How much gas there is follows from three numbers. The star's X-ray output is measured (Freund et al. (2022), A&A 664, A105). Its coronal temperature, 4.7 million kelvin, is not measured: it is the temperature stars of this X-ray output have (Johnstone & Güdel (2015), A&A 578, A129). Its mass loss, 23 times the Sun's, is not measured either: it is what the X-ray output suggests (Wood et al. (2021), ApJ 915, 37). Stars with a measured wind lie within a factor of 5 of that relation, and one is 38 times below it. Drawn out to 4 stellar radii in the star's own color; at each distance brightness is proportional to density.
